lines.text: I have an appointment with my dentist.
Many learners say: I have a date with my dentist.
Better: I have an appointment with my dentist.
A date is for a romantic meeting.
Appointment! I have an appointment with my dentist.

data.wrong: I have a date with my dentist.
data.right: I have an appointment with my dentist.
data.why: A date is for a romantic meeting.

quiz.stem: I have an ___ with my dentist.

native.tip: Im Deutschen sagen wir „Termin“ beim Zahnarzt. Im Englischen heißt das „appointment“, nicht „date“.

en.tip: German says “Termin.” English says “appointment” for a doctor, not “date.”
en.caption: Doctor visit? Say appointment! Wrong: “I have a date with my dentist.” Right: “I have an appointment with my dentist.” Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.
